issues.problem: lit 'the mind becomes (fixed on it)' misreads に: the idiom is something coming onto/into the mind, not the mind becoming something.
issues.action: Rewrote lit as 'to come onto the mind: something lands in your thoughts and stays there'.

issues.problem: ctx6 (個人情報の扱いには十分気をつける必要がある) fits 気を配る (ky107) just as well.
issues.action: Replaced with the polite announcement 「足元に気をつけてお降りください。」, where 気を配る cannot stand.

issues.problem: Cue and several contexts (e.g. 足を踏んでも謝らない人には…) fit 頭に来る (ky011) equally well.
issues.action: Cue now asks for calm, polite speech; replaced ctx2 with the polite complaint 「このような対応をされて、正直腹が立ちました。」 where casual 頭に来る is out of register. Contexts with 腹が立ってくる and 自分に腹が立つ kept as distinctive.

issues.problem: Misuse 1 (疲れが顔を出している) is not clearly wrong: figurative 顔を出す for something hidden emerging (弱気が顔を出す) is real usage. Also ctx6 (取引先へあいさつに顔を出した) fits 足を運ぶ (ky059) equally.
issues.action: Replaced misuse 1 with the particle error 会社の飲み会を顔を出した (the place takes に). Rewrote ctx6 with ついでに (dropping in while nearby), which rules out the deliberate trip of 足を運ぶ.
